questions.question: If the coordinates of a point are $(0, -4)$, then it lies
solutionSteps: A point $(x, y)$ with $x=0$ always lies on the Y-axis.
Since $x=0$ and $y=-4$, the point is on the negative Y-axis.

questions.question: The point which lies on y-axis at a distance of 5 units in the negative direction of y-axis is
solutionSteps: Point on y-axis has $x=0$.
Distance 5 in negative direction means $y=-5$.
So point is $(0, -5)$.

questions.question: The abscissa of a point is positive in
solutionSteps: Abscissa ($x$-coordinate) is positive to the right of the Y-axis.
This corresponds to Quadrants I and IV.

solutionSteps: Mirror image in x-axis keeps $x$ same and flips sign of $y$.

questions.question: Points $(-5, 2)$ and $(2, -5)$ lie in
solutionSteps: $(-, +)$ is Quadrant II. $(+, -)$ is Quadrant IV.
So they lie in II and IV respectively.

questions.question: Write the coordinates of the vertices of a rectangle whose length and breadth are 5 and 3 units respectively, one vertex at the origin, the longer side lies on the x-axis and one of the vertices lies in the third quadrant.
solutionSteps: Longer side (length 5) on x-axis in 3rd quadrant direction: $(-5, 0)$.
Breadth (3) in negative y direction: Vertex 3 $(-5, -3)$ and Vertex 4 $(0, -3)$.

questions.question: Plot the points $A(1, -1)$ and $B(4, 5)$. (i) Draw a line segment joining them. (ii) Write the coordinates of a point on this line segment between A and B.
solutionSteps: Points on line follow $y - (-1) = \frac{5 - (-1)}{4 - 1} (x - 1) \implies y+1 = 2(x-1) \implies y = 2x - 3$.
If $x=2$, $y=1$. So $(2, 1)$ is on the segment.
If $x=3$, $y=3$. So $(3, 3)$ is on the segment.

questions.question: Plot the points $P(-1, 0), Q(7, 0)$ and $R(7, 2)$. Find the coordinates of point $S$ such that $PQRS$ is a rectangle.
solutionSteps: $P(-1, 0)$ and $Q(7, 0)$ are on x-axis (length 8).
$R(7, 2)$ is 2 units above $Q$.
For $PQRS$ to be a rectangle, $S$ must be 2 units above $P$.
Coordinates of $S = (-1, 0+2) = (-1, 2)$.

questions.question: Find the area of the triangle whose vertices are $(0, 4), (0, 0)$ and $(3, 0)$.
solutionSteps: Vertices are on the axes. Base lies on x-axis from $(0,0)$ to $(3,0)$, so base = 3.
Height lies on y-axis from $(0,0)$ to $(0,4)$, so height = 4.
Area = $1/2 \times \text{base} \times \text{height} = 1/2 \times 3 \times 4 = 6$ square units.

questions.question: A point $P(2, 3)$ is reflected in the x-axis to $P'$. Then $P'$ is reflected in the y-axis to $P''$. Find the coordinates of $P''$. In which quadrant does $P''$ lie?
solutionSteps: Reflection of $(2, 3)$ in x-axis: sign of $y$ changes $\implies P'(2, -3)$.
Reflection of $(2, -3)$ in y-axis: sign of $x$ changes $\implies P''(-2, -3)$.
Since both coordinates are negative, $P''$ lies in Quadrant III.
